name: agreeing truces with rival rooms
gloss: Rooms already in contact end or forestall a fight with a truce: peace asked for, offered, agreed, honoured.
must_show: A pact to stop or avoid attacks between rooms already in contact: peace or a truce asked for, offered, agreed or celebrated; non-aggression pacts.
must_not_show: Lines and space settled where no fight began (T3-010); an alliance for joint defence or a joint fight (T3-150); a truce already made invoked against a breach (T3-195).
decide_when_both: A pact ending or forestalling a fight between rooms already in contact goes to T3-149; an agreement drawing borders or sharing space where no fight began goes to T3-010. A truce invoked against a breach is T3-195 when the invoking leads.

discriminators.question: Does the pact end or forestall a fight (T3-149), or settle lines where no fight began (T3-010)?
Do the rooms stop fighting each other (T3-149), or join to fight or defend together (T3-150)?
Is a truce made now (T3-149), or one already made invoked (T3-195)?
Does the room make peace with its own rival (T3-149), or keep out of a fight between others (T3-138)?
Is a fight ended or forestalled by a pact (T3-149), or help given in return for help (T3-151)?
Is a fight ended (T3-149), or two rival marks set together with no fight (T3-025)?
Is a fight on the canvas ended by truce (T3-149), or a quarrel made up (T3-047)?
Is a truce made (T3-149), or is cooperation argued as surrender (T3-193)?
Does a member act for the room toward another room as envoy or representative (T3-194), or is the truce itself asked for, offered or agreed (T3-149)?

varies: From a quick 'can we have peace here?' between rival universities to non-aggression pacts with the Void.
is_not: A border drawn between neighbours who never fought (T3-010).
two_or_half: It was split from T3-010 at B1b-06; it could merge back as deals between rooms, but a truce ends a fight, which a reader sees.

exemplars.quote: We're all on the same team here. Just request a truce.
The rivalry was fun, but I'm glad we had a truce in the end
A message of peace

name: forming alliances between rooms
gloss: Rooms join in an alliance for joint defence or a joint fight: alliances named, proposed, joined.
must_show: An alliance between rooms for defence or a fight: proposals and invitations, named alliances, rooms joining a front, promises to defend each other.
must_not_show: Help traded case by case (T3-151); help sent with nothing asked (T3-011); a small room relying on a bigger one (T3-099); a truce between rivals (T3-149).
decide_when_both: An alliance that trades help: T3-150 when joint defence or a fight is the frame, T3-151 when the swap of help is.

discriminators.question: Is help swapped case by case (T3-151), or a standing alliance for defence or a fight formed (T3-150)?
Do rivals stop fighting (T3-149), or rooms join to fight or defend (T3-150)?
Does a small room rely on a bigger one (T3-099), or do rooms ally (T3-150)?
Do kindred rooms make one joint mark (T3-056), or ally for defence or a fight (T3-150)?
Is loyalty professed to a colour faction (T3-174), or an alliance made between rooms (T3-150)?
Are the rooms allied for joint defence (T3-150), or is help sent to another's work (T3-011)?
Do the rooms join for defence or a fight (T3-150), or settle where their works meet (T3-010)?
Is an alliance formed for the fight (T3-150), or thanked and told afterwards (T3-072)?
Is friendship drawn between flags (T3-079), or an alliance for defence formed (T3-150)?
Does the room join a side (T3-150), or stay out (T3-138)?
Does a member act for the room toward another room as envoy or representative (T3-194), or is the alliance itself proposed, named or joined (T3-150)?
Is an agreement already made invoked, spread or said to be broken (T3-195), or a new alliance proposed, named or joined (T3-150)?

varies: From a two-room defence pact to a United Red Front of many subs.
is_not: Swapping repairs with a neighbour once (T3-151).
two_or_half: It was split from T3-010 at B1b-06; with T3-151 it could be one kind of mutual help, kept two because an alliance binds rooms beyond one swap.

name: bartering help with neighbours
gloss: Rooms trade help: repairs, defence, maintenance or room given in return for the same.
must_show: Help offered or asked in return for help: 'we'll help you move if you maintain ours', 'repay the favour', maintenance traded for room.
must_not_show: Help sent with nothing asked (T3-011); an alliance for joint defence (T3-150); a third room's work offered up in the bargain (T3-067).
decide_when_both: Help given in return is T3-151, help with nothing asked T3-011.

discriminators.question: Is help given in return (T3-151), or with nothing asked (T3-011)?
Is help swapped (T3-151), or a standing alliance formed (T3-150)?
Is help traded between two rooms alone (T3-151), or a third room's work offered up (T3-067)?
Is help traded (T3-151), or a line settled (T3-010)?
Is help traded by hand (T3-151), or one bot target pooled (T3-108)?
Is help given in return for help (T3-151), or a fight ended or forestalled by a pact (T3-149)?
Is help traded (T3-151), or the room's work adopted into a neighbour's (T3-071)?
Is help asked in return for help (T3-151), or asked outright (T3-084)?
Is protection repaid with help (T3-151), or relied on (T3-099)?
Does a member act for the room toward another room as envoy or representative (T3-194), or is the trade of help itself offered or agreed (T3-151)?
Is an agreement already made invoked, spread or said to be broken (T3-195), or a new trade of help offered or agreed (T3-151)?

varies: From a one-off swap of repairs to running exchanges of maintenance for room.
is_not: Sending pixels to a neighbour's defence unasked (T3-011).
two_or_half: See T3-011 and T3-150: the middle of three kinds of help between rooms, kept by whether the help is owed and whether it binds beyond the swap.

name: acting as envoys between rooms
gloss: A member acts for a room toward another room: envoy, diplomat, ambassador, representative, a proposal carried between threads.
must_show: A named role or errand between rooms: a member made the room's diplomat, a representative arriving in another room's thread, a council seat, a proposal carried from one room to another.
must_not_show: Members meeting other rooms in chat with no one acting for the room (T3-153); disputing who may speak for a room (T3-126); the deal itself (T3-010, T3-149, T3-150, T3-151).
decide_when_both: The envoy's errand is T3-194, the deal it carries T3-010 or its kin; when both have concepts of their own, the larger is primary.

discriminators.question: Does a member act for the room toward another (T3-194), or do members meet other rooms in chat (T3-153)?
Does a member act as envoy (T3-194), or is the right to speak for the room disputed (T3-126)?
Is the errand the doing (T3-194), or the line it settles (T3-010)?
Does the member act for their own room (T3-194), or go between two other rooms (T3-161)?
Is a member the room's envoy (T3-194), or is the language between rooms the problem met (T3-083)?

Does a member act for the room toward another room as envoy or representative (T3-194), or is the alliance itself proposed, named or joined (T3-150)?
Does a member act for the room toward another room as envoy or representative (T3-194), or is the trade of help itself offered or agreed (T3-151)?

varies: From one representative's arrival in a neighbour's thread to diplomats flaired on a council server across a dozen chats.
is_not: Members of two rooms chatting in a shared Discord (T3-153).
two_or_half: It was split from T3-010 at B1b-19-p2; it could be half of T3-153, contact between rooms, kept apart because a member holds the room's voice.

name: holding rooms to their agreements
gloss: Members invoke an agreement already made: its terms spread to placers, the room reminded to honour it, a neighbour accused of breach, a lapsed deal restored.
must_show: An existing agreement invoked: 'we made an agreement with hearts', 'it was the original deal', 'we agreed you can have the flower, but ...', a broken deal named.
must_not_show: A new deal made (T3-010, T3-149, T3-150, T3-151); an alliance's conduct or worth disputed, often after the close (T3-030); a member breaking the room's agreement (T3-102).
decide_when_both: A theme that makes a deal and later invokes it keeps the larger part as primary and adds the other under rule 0.

discriminators.question: Is an agreement made (T3-010), or one already made invoked (T3-195)?
Is a truce made (T3-149), or invoked against a breach (T3-195)?
Is the room held to its agreement so the work can go on (T3-195), or the alliance's conduct or worth disputed (T3-030)?
Is the agreement invoked (T3-195), or broken by a member (T3-102)?
Is another room held to an agreement (T3-195), or does an organised room say it does not control placers acting in its name (T3-188)?
Is another room held to an agreement (T3-195), or does the room stop its own attackers (T3-076)?
Is an agreement already made invoked, spread or said to be broken (T3-195), or a new alliance proposed, named or joined (T3-150)?
Is an agreement already made invoked, spread or said to be broken (T3-195), or a new trade of help offered or agreed (T3-151)?
Is an agreement already made invoked, spread or said to be broken (T3-195), or another room's work helped or defended, the pledge named only as the reason for the help (T3-011)?
Is an agreement already made invoked, spread or said to be broken (T3-195), or the room's own work defended, the pledge named only as the reason for the defence (T3-005)?

varies: From a quick 'no stop, we made an agreement' to accusations that a neighbour went over the logo after the deal.
is_not: Agreeing a new border with a neighbour (T3-010).
two_or_half: It was split from T3-010 at B1b-19-p2; it could merge back into the deal kinds, but invoking a deal already made is a different act from making one.

name: disputing how an alliance went
old_label: disputing an alliance after the close
gloss: Members dispute an alliance's conduct or worth, often after the close: who kept their word, betrayal, never again.
must_show: Argument over an alliance's or deal's conduct or worth: broken word alleged, betrayal warned of, collaboration renounced.
must_not_show: Holding a room to its agreement so the work can go on (T3-195); arguing whether cooperation is surrender (T3-193); blaming an attacker for a loss (T3-058).
decide_when_both: A breach named mid-work: T3-195; the alliance judged as a whole: T3-030.

discriminators.question: Is the agreement invoked so the work goes on (T3-195), or the alliance's conduct or worth disputed (T3-030)?
Is cooperation as such called surrender (T3-193), or one alliance's conduct disputed (T3-030)?
Is a rival blamed for a loss (T3-058), or an ally's conduct disputed (T3-030)?

varies: From 'that's the last time we collaborate with them' to warnings that a colour faction will betray its partner again.
is_not: Reminding a neighbour mid-work of the border agreed (T3-195).
two_or_half: It is half of T3-195, the same agreements judged; kept apart because the dispute weighs the alliance rather than invoking it.

name: making up with another sub
old_label: settling a quarrel with another sub
gloss: Two subs settle a quarrel: apologies, thanks and good wishes exchanged.
must_show: A quarrel between two subs closed by apology and acceptance, thanks or good wishes.
must_not_show: An apology for damage to a neighbour's work with repair offered (T3-040); a truce ending a fight on the canvas (T3-149).
decide_when_both: An apology for canvas damage that also closes a quarrel: T3-040 when the damage is the point, T3-047 when the quarrel is.

discriminators.question: Is damage to a neighbour's work apologised for (T3-040), or a quarrel between the subs closed (T3-047)?
Is a fight on the canvas ended by truce (T3-149), or a quarrel made up (T3-047)?
Are greetings sent with no quarrel behind them (T3-122), or a quarrel made up (T3-047)?
Is a quarrel made up in words (T3-047), or damage repaired by its makers (T3-119)?

varies: From 'sorry, we were a bit salty, good luck' to an attack claim turned into apology and help.

two_or_half: It could be half of T3-040, an apology between rooms; kept apart because the quarrel, not damage, is mended.

name: negotiating across a language gap

must_not_show: Writing in the room's own language to hide the plan (T3-116).
decide_when_both: A deal made across a language gap: the deal's kind is primary, T3-083 added when the gap has concepts of its own.

discriminators.question: Is language used to keep rivals out (T3-116), or a gap bridged to deal with another room (T3-083)?
Is a member the room's envoy (T3-194), or is the language between rooms the problem met (T3-083)?

varies: From one Google-translated reply to a member offering to translate for all non-Spanish helpers.

name: turning attackers into helpers
old_label: turning a former attacker into a helper
gloss: A room that attacked a work, or members of it, turn to help repair it.
must_show: Former attackers helping the work they damaged: admitting the damage and helping rebuild, repairing a work they overwrote, a takeover followed by help to rebuild elsewhere.
must_not_show: An apology with an offer of help not yet acted on (T3-040); help with no prior attack (T3-011).
decide_when_both: Apology and repair together: T3-119 when the former attackers act, T3-040 when they only apologise.

discriminators.question: Do the former attackers only apologise (T3-040), or help repair (T3-119)?
Is help sent with no prior attack (T3-011), or by those who attacked (T3-119)?
Is a quarrel made up in words (T3-047), or damage repaired by its makers (T3-119)?

varies: From one member who destroyed a figure helping bring it back to a room that took a spot by force and helped rebuild the work elsewhere.
is_not: An apology for damage with a promise to help later (T3-040).
two_or_half: It could be half of T3-040 and T3-011 together; kept apart because the helpers are the attackers.

must_not_show: Refusing a request for help on its own merits (T3-115); making peace with one's own rival (T3-149).
decide_when_both: Neutrality declared while making a truce with one side: T3-149 for the truce, T3-138 for the stance between others.

Does the member keep out of others' fight (T3-138), or help them reach terms (T3-161)?

decide_when_both: A truce argued over: T3-149 when the truce is made, T3-193 when its meaning as surrender is argued.

discriminators.question: Is a truce made (T3-149), or is cooperation argued as surrender (T3-193)?
